sanskrit: dāsyāmi bhavate kanyām iti pūrvaṃ nabhāṣitam ye caivāhur ye ca nāhur ye cāvaśyaṃ vadanty uta
english: "I shall give the maiden to you" — when this has not been declared beforehand, there are some who say it, some who do not, and some who must say it of necessity.

sanskrit: tasmād ā grahaṇāt pāṇer yācayanti parasparam kanyāvaraḥ purā datto marudbhir iti naḥ śrutam
english: Therefore, up until the taking of the hand, the two parties make request of one another. We have heard it told that in ancient times the bridegroom for a maiden was bestowed by the Maruts.

sanskrit: nāniṣṭāya pradātavyā kanyā ity ṛṣicoditam tan mūlaṃ kāmamūlasya prajanasyeti me matiḥ
english: "A maiden is not to be given to one undesired" — so the sages have enjoined. That, in my judgment, is the root of procreation, which itself is rooted in desire.

sanskrit: samīkṣya ca bahūn doṣān saṃvāsād vidviṣāṇayoḥ yathā niṣṭhākaraṃ śulkaṃ na jātv āsīt tathā śṛṇu
english: Having weighed well the many evils that arise from the cohabitation of two who hate each other, hear now how the bride-price never came to be a thing that settles the matter.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vicitravīryāya dve kanye samudāvaham jitvā ca māgadhān sarvān kāśīn atha ca kosalān gṛhītapāṇir ekāsīt prāptaśulkāparābhavat
english: For Vicitravīrya I brought home two maidens, after I had vanquished all the Māgadhas, the Kāśis, and the Kosalas. One had already had her hand taken in pledge, and being thus claimed, she met with rebuff.

sanskrit: pāṇau gṛhītā tatraiva visṛjyā iti me pitā abravīd itarāṃ kanyām āvahat sa tu kauravaḥ
english: "She whose hand has been taken must there and then be released," so my father said; and that scion of the Kurus took home only the other maiden.

sanskrit: apy anyām anupapraccha śaṅkamānaḥ pitur vacaḥ atīva hy asya dharmepsā pitur me 'bhyadhikābhavat
english: He inquired further about the other as well, being uncertain of his father's word; for his longing after dharma was exceedingly great — greater even than my father's.

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ rājann ācārepsur idaṃ vacaḥ ācāraṃ tattvato vettum icchāmīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then I myself, O king, desiring to know the right usage, spoke these words again and again: "I wish to understand the established practice in its very truth."

sanskrit: tato mayaivam ukte tu vākye dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ pitā mama mahārāja bāhlīko vākyam abravīt
english: When I had spoken thus, O great king, my father Bāhlika, foremost of those who uphold dharma, made this reply.

sanskrit: yadi vaḥ śulkato niṣṭhā na pāṇigrahaṇaṃ tathā lājāntaram upāsīta prāptaśulkā patiṃ vṛtam
english: "If for you the matter is settled by the bride-price and not by the taking of the hand, then let her for whom the price has been received attend upon the husband she has chosen, even up to the parched-grain rite."

sanskrit: na hi dharmavidaḥ prāhuḥ pramāṇaṃ vākyataḥ smṛtam yeṣāṃ vai śulkato niṣṭhā na pāṇigrahaṇāt tathā
english: "For those who know dharma do not declare that to be authoritative which rests on mere words alone — those, that is, for whom the matter is settled by the bride-price and not by the taking of the hand."

sanskrit: prasiddhaṃ bhāṣitaṃ dāne teṣāṃ pratyasanaṃ punaḥ ye manyante krayaṃ śulkaṃ na te dharmavido janāḥ
english: "What is openly spoken at the giving away is their rejoinder besides; but those who reckon the bride-price as a purchase — those folk do not know dharma."

sanskrit: na caitebhyaḥ pradātavyā na voḍhavyā tathāvidhā na hy eva bhāryā kretavyā na vikreyā kathaṃ cana
english: "To such men a maiden is not to be given, nor by them is one of that sort to be wedded; for a wife is in no wise to be bought, nor ever to be sold."

sanskrit: ye ca krīṇanti dāsīvad ye ca vikrīṇate janāḥ bhavet teṣāṃ tathā niṣṭhā lubdhānāṃ pāpacetasām
english: "Those folk who buy a woman as one buys a slave-girl, and those who sell — for such greedy men of sinful mind let the matter be settled in that fashion."

sanskrit: asmin dharme satyavantaṃ paryapṛcchanta vai janāḥ kanyāyāḥ prāptaśulkāyāḥ śulkadaḥ praśamaṃ gataḥ
english: On this point of dharma the people questioned Satyavān: "In the case of a maiden for whom the price has been received, the one who paid the price has died."

sanskrit: pāṇigrahītā cānyaḥ syād atra no dharmasaṃśayaḥ tan naś chindhi mahāprājña tvaṃ hi vai prājñasaṃmataḥ tattvaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ cakṣur bhavatu no bhavān
english: "And another would be the one to take her hand — herein lies our doubt concerning dharma. Resolve it for us, O greatly wise one, for you are esteemed among the wise; be you the eye for us who seek to know the truth."

sanskrit: tān evaṃ bruvataḥ sarvān satyavān vākyam abravīt yatreṣṭaṃ tatra deyā syān nātra kāryā vicāraṇā kurvate jīvato 'py evaṃ mṛte naivāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: To all of them speaking thus Satyavān made reply: "She is to be given where it is desired; herein no debate need be made. Men act so even while the man yet lives; when he is dead, there is no doubt at all."

sanskrit: devaraṃ praviśet kanyā tapyed vāpi mahat tapaḥ tam evānuvratā bhūtvā pāṇigrāhasya nāma sā
english: "Let the maiden go in unto the husband's brother, or else let her practice great austerity; remaining ever faithful to him alone, she bears the name of the one who took her hand."

sanskrit: likhanty eva tu keṣāṃ cid apareṣāṃ śanair api iti ye saṃvadanty atra ta etaṃ niścayaṃ viduḥ
english: "For some it is set down plainly in writing, for others only by degrees" — those who hold discourse together on this matter know this to be the settled conclusion.

sanskrit: tat pāṇigrahaṇāt pūrvam uttaraṃ yatra vartate sarvamaṅgalamantraṃ vai mṛṣāvādas tu pātakaḥ
english: Where a reply is given before the taking of the hand, that is indeed the all-auspicious sacred formula; but a false utterance is a cause of downfall.

sanskrit: pāṇigrahaṇamantrāṇāṃ niṣṭhā syāt saptame pade pāṇigrāhasya bhāryā syād yasya cādbhiḥ pradīyate
english: The consummation of the hand-taking formulas comes at the seventh step; she becomes the wife of the man who takes her hand, the man to whom she is given with the pouring of water.

sanskrit: anukūlām anuvaṃśāṃ bhrātrā dattām upāgnikām parikramya yathānyāyaṃ bhāryāṃ vinded dvijottamaḥ
english: Having circled the fire according to rule, the foremost of the twice-born wins as his wife one who is compliant, of suitable lineage, given by her brother, and led before the sacred fire.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kanyāyāḥ prāptaśulkāyāḥ patiś cen nāsti kaś cana tatra kā pratipattiḥ syāt tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If, for a maiden whose price has been received, there is no husband at all, what then should be the right procedure? Tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yāputrakasyāpy arikthasya pratipat sā tadā bhavet
english: Bhīṣma said: She would then have the standing of one without a son and without inheritance.

sanskrit: atha cet sāharec chulkaṃ krītā śulkapradasya sā tasyārthe 'patyam īheta yena nyāyena śaknuyāt
english: But if she should take the bride-price, she becomes, being bought, the woman of the one who paid it; for his sake let her seek to bear offspring by whatever lawful means she can.

sanskrit: na tasyā mantravat kāryaṃ kaś cit kurvīta kiṃ cana
english: For her let no one perform any rite whatsoever with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: svayaṃ vṛteti sāvitrī pitrā vai pratyapadyata tat tasyānye praśaṃsanti dharmajñā netare janāḥ
english: "She chose for herself" — thus Sāvitrī was accepted by her father; this some who know dharma commend, but other folk do not.

sanskrit: etat tu nāpare cakrur na pare jātu sādhavaḥ sādhūnāṃ punar ācāro garīyo dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Yet others did not do this, nor ever did the good men of old; and the conduct of the good is, moreover, the weightier mark of dharma.

sanskrit: asminn eva prakaraṇe sukratur vākyam abravīt naptā videharājasya janakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: On this very topic Sukratu spoke his word — the grandson of the great-souled Janaka, king of Videha.

sanskrit: asadācarite mārge kathaṃ syād anukīrtanam anupraśnaḥ saṃśayo vā satām etad upālabhet
english: "Upon a course of conduct that is wrong, how should there be praise, or further inquiry, or doubt? This the good would censure."

sanskrit: asad eva hi dharmasya pramādo dharma āsuraḥ nānuśuśruma jātv etām imāṃ pūrveṣu janmasu
english: "A lapse from dharma is itself a thing unworthy — a demonic dharma. Never have we heard of this manner of thing among men of bygone births."

sanskrit: bhāryāpatyor hi saṃbandhaḥ strīpuṃsos tulya eva saḥ ratiḥ sādhāraṇo dharma iti cāha sa pārthivaḥ
english: "For the bond of wife and husband, of woman and man, is one of equals; their delight is a dharma shared in common" — so spoke that prince.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atha kena pramāṇena puṃsām ādīyate dhanam putravad dhi pitus tasya kanyā bhavitum arhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Now by what rule is the wealth of men inherited? For a daughter ought to be to her father even as a son.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yathaivātmā tathā putraḥ putreṇa duhitā samā tasyām ātmani tiṣṭhantyāṃ katham anyo dhanaṃ haret
english: Bhīṣma said: As is one's own self, so is the son; and equal to the son is the daughter. While she, who is one's very self, yet stands, how should another carry off the wealth?

sanskrit: mātuś ca yautakaṃ yat syāt kumārībhāga eva saḥ dauhitra eva vā riktham aputrasya pitur haret
english: Whatever was the mother's marriage gift, that is the unmarried daughter's portion; or else the daughter's son may take the inheritance of a maternal grandfather who has no son.

sanskrit: dadāti hi sa piṇḍaṃ vai pitur mātāmahasya ca putradauhitrayor neha viśeṣo dharmataḥ smṛtaḥ
english: For he offers the funeral rice-ball both to his own father and to his maternal grandfather; between a son and a daughter's son no distinction is here declared in point of dharma.

sanskrit: anyatra jātayā sā hi prajayā putra īhate duhitānyatra jātena putreṇāpi viśiṣyate
english: For by offspring born elsewhere a man seeks as it were a son; and a daughter, through a son born elsewhere of her, is even more distinguished.

sanskrit: dauhitrakeṇa dharmeṇa nātra paśyāmi kāraṇam vikrītāsu ca ye putrā bhavanti pitur eva te
english: By the rule of the daughter's son I see herein no cause for distinction; and the sons born of women who have been sold belong to the father alone.

sanskrit: asūyavas tv adharmiṣṭhāḥ parasvādāyinaḥ śaṭhāḥ āsurād adhisaṃbhūtā dharmād viṣamavṛttayaḥ
english: But envious, most unrighteous, seizers of others' goods, and deceitful are they — sprung from the demonic mode of marriage, crooked of conduct in matters of dharma.

sanskrit: atra gāthā yamodgītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ dharmajñā dharmaśāstreṣu nibaddhā dharmasetuṣu
english: On this point those versed in ancient lore, knowers of dharma, recite the verses chanted by Yama, set down in the treatises of dharma, in the bulwarks of dharma.

sanskrit: yo manuṣyaḥ svakaṃ putraṃ vikrīya dhanam icchati kanyāṃ vā jīvitārthāya yaḥ śulkena prayacchati
english: Whatever man sells his own son and desires wealth thereby, or who for the sake of a livelihood gives away his daughter for a price —

sanskrit: saptāvare mahāghore niraye kālasāhvaye svedaṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ ca tasmin preta upāśnute
english: in the seventh and lowest, most terrible hell called Kāla, that departed one feeds, in that place, on sweat, urine, and dung.

sanskrit: ārṣe gomithunaṃ śulkaṃ ke cid āhur mṛṣaiva tat alpaṃ vā bahu vā rājan vikrayas tāvad eva saḥ
english: In the sage's marriage some call the pair of cattle a bride-price; but that is false. Whether little or much, O king, such a thing is just so much a sale.

sanskrit: yady apy ācaritaḥ kaiś cin naiṣa dharmaḥ kathaṃ cana anyeṣām api dṛśyante lobhataḥ saṃpravṛttayaḥ
english: Even though it has been practiced by some, this is in no wise dharma; and the practices of still others too are seen to spring from greed.

sanskrit: vaśyāṃ kumārīṃ vihitāṃ ye ca tām upabhuñjate ete pāpasya kartāras tamasy andhe 'tha śerate
english: And those who enjoy a maiden who is set apart as their dependent — these are doers of sin, and they lie thereafter in blind darkness.

sanskrit: anyo 'py atha na vikreyo manuṣyaḥ kiṃ punaḥ prajāḥ adharmamūlair hi dhanair na tair artho 'sti kaś cana
english: Nay, any other human being too is not to be sold — how much less one's own offspring! For of wealth rooted in unrighteousness there is no profit whatsoever.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca prācetasasya vacanaṃ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ yasyāḥ kiṃ cin nādadate jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Those versed in ancient lore recite the saying of Pracetas' son: where the kinsmen take nothing for a maiden, that is no sale.

sanskrit: arhaṇaṃ tat kumārīṇām ānṛśaṃsyatamaṃ ca tat sarvaṃ ca pratideyaṃ syāt kanyāyai tad aśeṣataḥ
english: That is the honoring due to maidens, and that the most free from cruelty; and all of it should be given back to the maiden, without remainder.

sanskrit: pitṛbhir bhrātṛbhiś caiva śvaśurair atha devaraiḥ pūjyā lālayitavyāś ca bahukalyāṇam īpsubhiḥ
english: By fathers and brothers, by fathers-in-law and husbands' brothers, women should be honored and cherished by those who desire great welfare.

sanskrit: yadi vai strī na roceta pumāṃsaṃ na pramodayet amodanāt punaḥ puṃsaḥ prajanaṃ na pravardhate
english: If a woman take no pleasure and do not gladden the man, then from the man's lack of gladness procreation does not increase.

sanskrit: pūjyā lālayitavyāś ca striyo nityaṃ janādhipa apūjitāś ca yatraitāḥ sarvās tatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ tadaiva tat kulaṃ nāsti yadā śocanti jāmayaḥ
english: Women are ever to be honored and cherished, O ruler of men; and where they go unhonored, there all rites are fruitless. That house ceases to be a house in the very hour when its women grieve.

sanskrit: jāmīśaptāni gehāni nikṛttānīva kṛtyayā naiva bhānti na vardhante śriyā hīnāni pārthiva
english: Houses cursed by their women, as though cut down by a sorcerer's spell, neither shine nor prosper, being bereft of fortune, O prince.

sanskrit: striyaḥ puṃsāṃ paridade manur jigamiṣur divam abalāḥ svalpakaupīnāḥ suhṛdaḥ satyajiṣṇavaḥ
english: Manu, when about to depart for heaven, entrusted women to the keeping of men — the weak ones, scant in covering, kindly, ever winning by their truth.

sanskrit: īrṣyavo mānakāmāś ca caṇḍā asuhṛdo 'budhāḥ striyo mānanam arhanti tā mānayata mānavāḥ
english: Jealous, eager for honor, fierce, unfriendly, and unknowing though they be — women deserve honor; honor them, O men.

sanskrit: strīpratyayo hi vo dharmo ratibhogāś ca kevalāḥ paricaryānnasaṃskārās tadāyattā bhavantu vaḥ
english: For your dharma rests upon women, and your delights and enjoyments wholly so; let the service, the food, and the consecrations be dependent upon them for you.

sanskrit: utpādanam apatyasya jātasya paripālanam prītyarthaṃ lokayātrā ca paśyata strīnibandhanam
english: The begetting of offspring, the rearing of what is born, and the daily course of the world for the sake of joy — behold, all this is bound up with women.

sanskrit: saṃmānyamānāś caitābhiḥ sarvakāryāṇy avāpsyatha videharājaduhitā cātra ślokam agāyata
english: And by these, when they are duly honored, you shall attain all your aims. On this the daughter of the king of Videha sang a verse.

sanskrit: nāsti yajñaḥ striyaḥ kaś cin na śrāddhaṃ nopavāsakam dharmas tu bhartṛśuśrūṣā tayā svargaṃ jayaty uta
english: "For a woman there is no sacrifice, no rite for the ancestors, no fasting; her dharma is service to her husband, and by that she wins heaven."

sanskrit: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane putrās tu sthavirībhāve na strī svātantryam arhati
english: "The father protects her in girlhood, the husband protects her in youth, and the sons in old age; a woman is not fit for independence."

sanskrit: śriya etāḥ striyo nāma satkāryā bhūtim icchatā lālitā nigṛhītā ca strī śrīr bhavati bhārata
english: These women are very Fortune herself; they are to be well treated by one who desires prosperity. A woman, when cherished and yet held in check, becomes Śrī, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sarvaśāstravidhānajña rājadharmārthavittama atīva saṃśayacchettā bhavān vai prathitaḥ kṣitau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O you who know the ordinances of all the treatises, best knower of the duties and aims of kings, you are renowned throughout the earth as one who cuts away doubt utterly.

sanskrit: kaś cit tu saṃśayo me 'sti tan me brūhi pitāmaha asyām āpadi kaṣṭāyām anyaṃ pṛcchāma kaṃ vayam
english: A certain doubt is mine; tell me of it, O grandfather. In this grievous time of distress, whom else should we ask?

sanskrit: yathā nareṇa kartavyaṃ yaś ca dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ etat sarvaṃ mahābāho bhavān vyākhyātum arhati
english: What a man ought to do, and what is the eternal dharma — all this, O mighty-armed one, you are able to expound.

sanskrit: catasro vihitā bhāryā brāhmaṇasya pitāmaha brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrā ca ratim icchataḥ
english: Four wives are ordained for a brāhmaṇa, O grandfather, if he desires their company — a brāhmaṇī, a kṣatriyā, a vaiśyā, and a śūdrā.

sanskrit: tatra jāteṣu putreṣu sarvāsāṃ kurusattama ānupūrvyeṇa kas teṣāṃ pitryaṃ dāyādyam arhati
english: Among the sons born of all these, O best of the Kurus, which of them, in due order, is entitled to the paternal inheritance?

sanskrit: kena vā kiṃ tato hāryaṃ pitṛvittāt pitāmaha etad icchāmi kathitaṃ vibhāgas teṣu yaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: And by which of them, and how much, is to be taken from the father's wealth, O grandfather? I wish this to be told — what division among them is laid down.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyas trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ eteṣu vihito dharmo brāhmaṇasya yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: The brāhmaṇa, the kṣatriya, and the vaiśya — these three varṇas are the twice-born; among these is the rule ordained for the brāhmaṇa, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vaiṣamyād atha vā lobhāt kāmād vāpi paraṃtapa brāhmaṇasya bhavec chūdrā na tu dṛṣṭāntataḥ smṛtā
english: Through irregularity, or through greed, or through desire, O scorcher of foes, a brāhmaṇa may come to have a śūdra wife; but she is not approved by any sound precedent.

sanskrit: śūdrāṃ śayanam āropya brāhmaṇaḥ pīḍito bhavet prāyaścittīyate cāpi vidhidṛṣṭena hetunā
english: A brāhmaṇa who raises a śūdra woman to his bed becomes thereby defiled, and must perform expiation by a means prescribed in the rules.

sanskrit: tatra jāteṣv apatyeṣu dviguṇaṃ syād yudhiṣṭhira atas te niyamaṃ vitte saṃpravakṣyāmi bhārata
english: And if children are born of her, the expiation would be twofold, O Yudhiṣṭhira. Hence I shall now declare to you the rule concerning the wealth, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇyo govṛṣo yānaṃ yat pradhānatamaṃ bhavet brāhmaṇyās tad dharet putra ekāṃśaṃ vai pitur dhanāt
english: An auspicious bull marked with good signs, and whatever conveyance is most excellent — these the son of the brāhmaṇī shall take as a single share, over and above, from the father's wealth.

sanskrit: śeṣaṃ tu daśadhā kāryaṃ brāhmaṇasvaṃ yudhiṣṭhira tatra tenaiva hartavyāś catvāro 'ṃśāḥ pitur dhanāt
english: But the remainder of the brāhmaṇa's property is to be made into ten parts, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and of these the same son shall take four shares of the father's wealth.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāyās tu yaḥ putro brāhmaṇaḥ so 'py asaṃśayaḥ sa tu mātṛviśeṣeṇa trīn aṃśān hartum arhati
english: The son of the kṣatriyā wife is also a brāhmaṇa, beyond all doubt; but by reason of the difference in his mother he is entitled to take three shares.

sanskrit: varṇe tṛtīye jātas tu vaiśyāyāṃ brāhmaṇād api dviraṃśas tena hartavyo brāhmaṇasvād yudhiṣṭhira
english: And he who is born in the third varṇa, of a vaiśyā by a brāhmaṇa, shall take two shares of the brāhmaṇa's property, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śūdrāyāṃ brāhmaṇāj jāto nityādeyadhanaḥ smṛtaḥ alpaṃ vāpi pradātavyaṃ śūdrāputrāya bhārata
english: The one born of a śūdra woman by a brāhmaṇa is declared to be one whose share of wealth is not fixed by right; yet at least a little is to be given to the son of the śūdra woman, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: daśadhā pravibhaktasya dhanasyaiṣa bhavet kramaḥ savarṇāsu tu jātānāṃ samān bhāgān prakalpayet
english: This would be the order for wealth divided into ten parts. But for sons born of wives of the same varṇa one should allot equal shares.

sanskrit: abrāhmaṇaṃ tu manyante śūdrāputram anaipuṇāt triṣu varṇeṣu jāto hi brāhmaṇād brāhmaṇo bhavet
english: The son of a śūdra woman they reckon, owing to his lack of fitness, as no brāhmaṇa; for one born of a brāhmaṇa in the three varṇas becomes a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: smṛtā varṇāś ca catvāraḥ pañcamo nādhigamyate haret tu daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ śūdrāputraḥ pitur dhanāt
english: Four varṇas are declared, and no fifth is recognized; yet the son of a śūdra woman may take a tenth part of the father's wealth.

sanskrit: tat tu dattaṃ haret pitrā nādattaṃ hartum arhati avaśyaṃ hi dhanaṃ deyaṃ śūdrāputrāya bhārata
english: But that he may take only if it has been given by the father; what is not given he is not entitled to take. Yet of necessity some wealth must be given to the son of the śūdra woman, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharma iti tasmai pradīyate yatra tatra samutpanno guṇāyaivopakalpate
english: "Freedom from cruelty is the highest dharma" — therefore it is given to him; and wherever he may have been born, it serves only to his benefit.
